'''Balosar''' was a [[Planet/Legends|planet]] in the [[Core Worlds/Legends|Core Worlds]], and home to the [[Balosar (species)/Legends|Balosar]] [[Species/Legends|species]]. It was a polluted, poverty-stricken world of grimy factories and downtrodden people, and a place where tourism was discouraged. Such an environment encouraged many of the native Balosars to become criminals.

==Description==
A highly industrialized world, the towers of Balosar rose so high that light could not penetrate deep enough to reach the surface. The suffocating amount of air pollution was so dense that the air was barely breathable, forcing the native Balosars to adapt to filter out poisonous substances from their bloodstream. Under the surface of the planet, the crust was pocked with cave systems which protected the [[Balo mushroom/Legends|balo mushrooms]] from the polluted surface.<ref name="NEGAS" />

==History==
[[File:Battle_of_the_Balosar_system.png|thumb|left|A battle rages over Balosar during the [[Cold War (Galactic Republic–Sith Empire)|Cold War]].]]
Located in the [[Core Worlds/Legends|Core Worlds]], the industrialized planet Balosar was discovered by the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] during the [[Great Manifest Period/Legends|Great Manifest Period]] and joined the [[Corellian Hegemony]] during the [[Alsakan Conflicts/Legends|Alsakan Conflicts]], as the [[Star system/Legends|star systems]] declared not to get involved in the fighting. As the conflict passed, Balosar managed to avoid much of the affairs of the greater galaxy, as their home government became more and more corrupt.<ref name="TEGTW">''[[The Essential Guide to Warfare]]''</ref> As the planet's industry grew larger, Balosar's regulations on pollution were whittled down to nothing as corporate interests gained greater control. As more and more interstellar corporations opened factories on the planet and employed the natives for low wages, the planet attracted the attention of many relief groups from across the Republic. Despite the interests of these groups, they had little luck gaining traction on the world due to the corruption of the government.<ref name="NEGAS" />

The economy on Balosar eventually came to a standstill, resulting in the government cuts to education. Many families who are offered scholarships quickly send their children offworld to help them become more successful then they could ever be on their homeworld. As education crumbled, the natives of Balosar quickly devolved into criminal activity. The government began to harvest the [[Balo mushroom/Legends|balo mushrooms]] which grew in underground caves protected from the air pollution on the surface. Using the [[Ixetal cilona/Legends|Ixetal cilona]] extracted from the mushrooms, government factories produced [[Death stick/Legends|death sticks]] en masse and export them throughout [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]]. Becoming highly competitive with the narcotic [[Ryll/Legends|ryll]] on the [[Spice/Legends|spice]] market, the Balosars earned the enduring dislike from their drug rivals, the [[Twi'lek/Legends|Twi'leks]] of [[Ryloth/Legends|Ryloth]].<ref name="NEGAS" />

In the wake of the [[Great Galactic War]], Balosar was the site of a space battle towards the end of the [[Cold War (Galactic Republic–Sith Empire)|Cold War]]. The [[Sith Empire (Post–Great Hyperspace War)|Sith Empire]], in their effort to destroy the Republic, constructed an illegal [[Balosar Outpost|outpost]] over the planet as a staging ground for assaults on the Republic. Upon its discovery, it was the site of a [[Battle of the Balosar system|massive battle]].<ref name="TOR">{{TORcite|type=space|Balosar Outpost}}</ref>

During the conflict with the [[Eternal Empire]], an abandoned [[Smuggler/Legends|smuggling]] vessel was rediscovered near Balosar filled with priceless cargo.<ref name="Mission">{{TORcite|type=crewskill|Underworld Trading|Finders Keepers}}</ref>

[[File:Balosar-NEGAS.png|thumb|150px|A [[Balosar (species)/Legends|Balosar]].]]

When the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]] erupted between the Republic and the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Confederacy of Independent Systems]], Balosar remained in the Republic's control as the [[Twentieth Army|20th Sector Army]] of the [[Grand Army of the Republic/Legends|Grand Army of the Republic]] protected the world from invasion.<ref name="TEGTW" /> When the Republic fell to the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]], Balosar had no choice but to declare allegiance to [[Emperor/Legends|Emperor]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]] and managed to avoid involvement in the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]]. When the Empire began to fracture with the rise of the [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]], Balosar refused to align with either side, preferring to remain neutral as war ravaged other planets in the Core. Around that time, Balosar suffered a major setback as air pollution reached such a height that it managed to infiltrate the underground balo farms, poisoning the crops and the stored spores. As a result of this devastation, ryll was able to take over the drug market, gaining a monopoly in the narcotic industry. Joining with Twi'lek dealers to support their economy, the planet avoided the [[Yuuzhan Vong War|tide of war]] brought by the [[Yuuzhan Vong]] through pure virtue of the fact that the Yuuzhan Vong were drawn elsewhere to defend themselves from the [[Galactic Federation of Free Alliances|Galactic Alliance]] before they could attack the planet.<ref name="NEGAS" />

As of [[137 ABY]], Balosar was located within the [[Core Worlds Security Zone]] of the [[Darth Krayt's Galactic Empire|Empire]] of [[Darth Krayt]].<ref name="TEA" />
